oracles.claim: For a valid ML-KEM key pair, Decaps(dk, Encaps(ek).ciphertext) shall equal Encaps(ek).shared_secret.
limitations: Round-trip agreement is a functional relation, not an IND-CCA security result
Finite testing cannot establish computational security

controls.positive_control: distinct randomness produces a distinct ciphertext
controls.negative_control: a valid encapsulation always decapsulates on the same implementation

oracles.claim: Two conforming ML-KEM implementations exchanging encapsulation keys and ciphertexts shall derive the same shared secret.
limitations: Requires the pair file to declare a compatible exchange contract
A self-reference pair does not establish independent correctness

controls.positive_control: left-to-right and right-to-left exchange both reconstruct the encapsulated secret
controls.negative_control: local round trips succeed on both implementations

oracles.claim: A correctly sized ciphertext whose re-encryption does not match shall not yield the original encapsulated shared secret.
limitations: Does not prove IND-CCA security
Fallback stability, z-separation, and no-reject-flag behavior require the dedicated implicit-rejection relations

controls.positive_control: the unmodified ciphertext decapsulates to the encapsulated secret
controls.negative_control: the mutation record shows the ciphertext bytes changed

oracles.claim: ML-KEM key generation and encapsulation shall consume the supplied randomness so that distinct randomness streams produce distinct outputs.
limitations: Does not test reported RNG failure handling (no output on failure)
Does not measure RBG health or entropy quality

controls.positive_control: two distinct deterministic tapes are observed to be consumed

oracles.claim: For a correctly sized invalid ML-KEM ciphertext, decapsulation shall return a stable implicit-rejection secret that depends on the stored rejection secret z, while valid decapsulation shall not depend on z, and no public reject flag shall be exposed.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 203 Sections 7.3 and 3.3; DeepSeek design doc Section 24 (implicit-rejection relations)
limitations: Does not prove IND-CCA security
A semantically neutral ciphertext mutation is recorded as no_effect rather than a finding

controls.positive_control: the untouched valid ciphertext decapsulates to the encapsulated secret
controls.negative_control: the mutation records show both the ciphertext and the z region changed

oracles.claim: Exact ciphertext length enforcement for ML-KEM decapsulation is required by FIPS 203, but the raw fixed-pointer API used here has no ciphertext length parameter; enforcement must be provided by a length-aware wrapper.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 203 Section 7.3; DeepSeek design doc Section 19 (length oracle boundary)
limitations: The fixed-pointer raw boundary cannot perform runtime length validation; this record is NOT_APPLICABLE, not a pass
A wrapper-level exact-length oracle requires a length-aware adapter

controls.negative_control: the record is not persisted as a security finding

oracles.claim: ML-KEM encapsulation shall not proceed on an encapsulation key whose 12-bit polynomial coefficients are not canonical: q-1 is accepted, and q, q+1, and 4095 are rejected before encapsulation.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 203 Sections 7.2 and 4.2 (encapsulation-key checks); DeepSeek design doc Sections 28.4 and 44
limitations: Boundary positions sample the first, middle, and last coefficient of every polynomial plus a byte-straddling pair
A wrapper that normalizes or reduces coefficients before encapsulation records accepted behavior as a finding

controls.negative_control: each mutation record shows the encoded coefficient changed to the boundary value

oracles.claim: ML-KEM.KeyGen_internal(d, z) shall produce byte-identical ek and dk values for the NIST ACVP ML-KEM keyGen vectors.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 203 Section 6.1 and Algorithm 16; NIST ACVP ML-KEM-keyGen-FIPS203 expectedResults
limitations: The checked-in table is a capped subset of the ACVP corpus
Requires a pinned ACVP-Server commit and the reference adapter derand hook

controls.positive_control: a second run with the same d and z is byte-identical
controls.negative_control: distinct d/z inputs produce distinct keys

oracles.claim: ML-KEM.Encaps_internal(ek, m) shall produce the ACVP expected ciphertext c and shared secret k.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 203 Section 6.2 and Algorithm 17; NIST ACVP ML-KEM-encapDecap-FIPS203 expectedResults
limitations: Capped ACVP subset; requires the reference adapter encaps_derand hook

controls.positive_control: the same deterministic coins reproduce the same ciphertext
controls.negative_control: the baseline public key is a fixed ACVP vector

oracles.claim: ML-KEM.Decaps(dk, c) shall produce the ACVP expected shared secret k.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 203 Section 6.3 and Algorithm 18; NIST ACVP ML-KEM-encapDecap-FIPS203 expectedResults
limitations: Capped ACVP subset

controls.positive_control: the expected shared secret equals the encaps vector k
controls.negative_control: a different ciphertext changes the derived secret

oracles.claim: A reported RNG failure during ML-KEM key generation or encapsulation should produce a failure indication and no cryptographic output rather than proceeding with zeroed randomness.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 203 Section 3.3 and DeepSeek design doc Sections 22 and 28.9
limitations: Void randombytes APIs cannot report failure; continuing with zeroed coins is a hardening gap, not a normative nonconformance
The fault injector signals failure through the PQCFuzz RNG layer, not through the operating-system RNG

controls.positive_control: the same call succeeds without the injected failure
controls.negative_control: the failure tape is observed to be consumed

oracles.claim: When an allocation fails during ML-KEM key generation, the call should report a failure and leave caller output buffers untouched, with no partial key material exposed.
oracles.source_reference: DeepSeek design doc Sections 25 and 36.7 (allocator fault injector and failure-state contract)
limitations: Requires a binary built with -Wl,--wrap=malloc/calloc/realloc
Libraries that do not document allocation-failure behavior are reported as HARDENING_GAP, not as normative nonconformance

controls.positive_control: key generation succeeds without injected allocation failure
controls.negative_control: each subtest records the number of triggered allocation failures
